role: Senior Business Intelligence Engineer, Prime Video Partner Experience & Supply Chain
responsibilities: Lead the design, implementation, and delivery of BI solutions in complex and/or ambiguous problem areas, taking the long-term view of how each solution fits the team's architecture and lifecycle, and proactively fixing architecture deficiencies
Own and influence data lineage across the organization, from how data is generated through how metrics are aggregated to how business intelligence is consumed and acted upon
Lead large, multi-person BI projects: decompose them into parallel workstreams for yourself and other data professionals, and reassemble the work into a cohesive, successful launch

Drive BI engineering best practices and set standards for the org (operational excellence, code reviews, syntax and naming conventions, metric definitions, alarms); ensure solutions are accurate, timely, accessible, and actionable
Build inventive, robust, scalable, and extensible data pipelines, data models, and dashboards from multi-dimensional datasets that others can easily maintain and build upon
Resolve the root cause of pervasive or persistent problems, influencing decisions across teams and building consensus to find and drive the best path forward

Understand and articulate the capabilities and limitations of the systems you work with (e.g., cluster size, concurrent users, data classification) to both technical and non-technical audiences, clarifying what is possible today versus what requires technology investment

Build fast prototypes using Amazon AI tools (Kiro, Claude CLI, QuickSuite) and translate them into production-grade data products, selecting optimal tools by balancing speed, efficiency, and scalability
Present insights and recommendations to senior stakeholders verbally and in writing, and influence their decisions and future requirements

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Drive BI engineering best practices and set standards for the org (operational excellence, code reviews, syntax and naming conventions, metric definitions, alarms); ensure solutions are accurate, timely, accessible, and actionable
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Standards, alarms, accuracy, root-cause fixes and trusted insights outnumber the speed phrases ("fast-paced", "Build fast prototypes") by more than two to one. This is a different team from the four 2026-10-05 Prime Video records.
evidence.domain_risk: Where are the systemic bottlenecks slowing content delivery
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Content supply-chain analytics affects business decisions without regulatory or financial-reporting language, so it is moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: We are part of the central Product and Data Team within the Partner Experience & Supply Chain organization at Prime Video.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A central data team inside a large organisation, running multi-person BI projects across several data professionals, is an established function at scale.
evidence.jd_authorship: Build fast prototypes using Amazon AI tools (Kiro, Claude CLI, QuickSuite) and translate them into production-grade data products
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Some bullets are specific (named AI tools, alarms, naming conventions), but most use Amazon's standard BI leveling language, so it is mixed.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: working with limited guidance alongside product managers, engineers, and operations leaders
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Product, engineering and supply-chain operations audiences get equal weight, so it is mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: you will shape the analytics strategy for the org, decide where to invest, and lead large initiatives
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns BI architecture and lineage, sets org standards and leads multi-person projects.
evidence.ai_role: Build fast prototypes using Amazon AI tools (Kiro, Claude CLI, QuickSuite)
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate uses AI coding tools to prototype their own work, so it is ai_user.
evidence.testing_framing: ensure solutions are accurate, timely, accessible, and actionable
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Accuracy, alarms and standards are things the candidate ensures and sets in the responsibilities.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: How do we predict and prevent supply chain issues before they impact customers?
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Operational problems and root causes are the concern, secondary to delivering insight, so it is moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Fixing existing architecture runs alongside building new pipelines, models and prototypes.
evidence.loss_aversion: prevent supply chain issues before they impact customers — operational, secondary to delivery.
